lines.speaker: d
lines.text: In September twenty twenty-six, a Cold War spy satellite broke apart in orbit, and nobody will say why.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: On September thirteenth, the Space Force confirmed it had fragmented, about seven hundred seventy-five kilometres up.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: No cause. No official count of the pieces.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: It was called U S A thirty-two. A Titan Two rocket lifted it from California in nineteen eighty-eight.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Analysts say it was Farrah Three, built to listen to Soviet radar. Yes, the name matches the actress.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Online, people asked if it was shot down on purpose. No government has said that.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Analysts suggest something duller: an old battery or fuel tank may simply have ruptured.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Or a tiny piece of untracked debris hit it, in one of the busiest orbits above Earth.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: One modelling firm estimates roughly thirty-five hundred fragments bigger than a centimetre.
